Bench: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Anil Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Nikhil Chaturvedi
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1. Heard Mr Arvind Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Mr Vinay Saran, learned Senior
Advocate assisted by Mr Nikhil Chaturvedi, learned counsel for the informant, Thakur Azad Singh,
learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed today and the same is taken on record.
In compliance of the order dated 14.07.2023, Mr Deependra Shankar Agarwal, the applicant, is present in person before the Court duly identified by his counsel.

sentences.text: 3. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 336 of 2020, under sections 409/420 IPC, P.S. New Agra, District Agra during the pendency of investigation.

4. As per averments made in the FIR, informant, namely, Rachit Agarwal, who is Director and 40%
Shareholder of a Company in the name and style of M/s Madhusudan Vehicles Private Limited,
which was was formed in the year 2011, and since then the applicant Deependra Shankar Agarwal is also a Director in the said company along with the informant.
The said company is said to be involved in sales of vehicles of Maruti Suzuki India Ltd. and also engaged in services of the vehicles manufactured by Maruti Suzuki India Ltd.

It is also alleged that both the Directors of the Company,
namely, the applicant and the informant are committed to protect the interests of the shareholders of the said Company and both cannot take any personal benefit without the consent and knowledge of each others.

But the applicant, taking the advantage of nationwide lock-down due to novel corona virus pandemic, and without the knowledge of the Board or the informant, or the company or without any approval of any kind from the said company, is said to have transferred a sum of Rs.
78,00,000/- to his own account from Company's Bank Account number 35257296278, which is said operative in State Bank of India, through cheque possessed by him, by misappropriating the cheque number 527428 of the said bank account of the company, with the intention of causing wrongful loss to its shareholders and the informant, and thereby applicant is said to have embezelled a sum of Rs. 78,00,000/- and also caused wrongful loss to the said Company.

It is also alleged that when the informant repeatedly tried to talk to the applicant, he was not ready to talk, and therefore, it became clear that the applicant had deliberately committed the said criminal act under his well thought plan.

It is further alleged that a legal notice was sent to the applicant on 5.5.2020 but he failed to return the said amount to the company and further applicant on the basis of its false facts replied to the said notice stating that the said amount was paid to him as advance money for purchase of his property by the said Company and in terms of the agreement applicant is further required to be paid a sum of Rs. 40 Lacs more and in case the said amount is not paid, the amount taken as advance shall be confiscated.
It is also alleged that there was no such agreement by the said Company nor there exists any such proposal or the company is in need of the said property.

It is thus alleged that the applicant misusing his position of Directorship of the Company for his own personal use with a dishonest intention embezelled and misappropriated the said amount of the Company without the knowledge of the informant or the Board of the Company.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has apprehension of arrest in the above mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence collected to connect him with the alleged crime.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.

It is further contended that with regard to the allegations levelled against the applicant, the informant is said to have approached the Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad being Company Petition No. 171 of 2020 (Rachit Agarwal Vs Madhusudan Vehicles Pvt Ltd and others.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the Investigating Officer after conducting elaborate investigation earlier submitted final report in the matter on 26.10.2020.

Against which protest petition was filed and learned CJM, Agra vide order dated 15.03.2022 rejected the said final report and directed the police to further probe into the matter and since then matter is under investigation.

It is further submitted that the matter relates to purely of civil dispute and no criminal case is made out against the applicant and the present proceeding is Deependra Shanker Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157835452/
2 nothing but to harass the applicant and send him behind the jail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the applicant is co-operating with the investigation, therefore, there is no requirement of custodial interrogation.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further contended that the applicant himself has filed a Company Petition No. 172 of 2020 under the Companies Act, 2013 against the informant for mismanagement of the Company and the said matter is still pending before the Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad and the informant is contesting the said matter before lodging of the FIR,
therefore no criminal case is made out against the applicant.
He has explained the criminal history of six cases levelled against him in the rejoinder affidavit.
7. Learned counsel for the informant as well as learned AGA have opposed the prayer for bail.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the informant that applicant is habitual in committing similar type of offences of cheating and forgery and has accumulated wealth by criminal means not only by cheating different banks and financial institutions, who have initiated recovery proceedings against him.
He has pointed out that there are six criminal cases against the applicant.
It is further submitted that there is every likelihood that applicant would abscond not only in the present case but also in others criminal and civil cases pending against him.

It is further submitted that the intention of the applicant to commit the offence is apparent as there is no document on record either in the shape of the Board resolution or any sort of agreement or agreement to sale the property as claimed by the applicant and further the alleged property, claimed to be purchased by the informant or his company in the defence set up by the applicant, was already mortgaged with UCO Bank Belanganj, Agra long before April 2020.
It is further submitted that mere filing of Company petition or any proceedings before any Tribunal cannot absolve the applicant from liability and the dispute cannot be termed as Civil litigation.

It is further submitted that the investigation in the case is still not completed and if the applicant is granted anticipatory bail, there is every likelihood of the tampering with the material evidence and witnesses.
8.
It has been settled in plethora of decisions that while considering an application for bail, detailed discussion of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits is to be avoided.
The facts in the present case are that there is some evidence that the applicant is said to be involved in the admitted fraud and misappropriation of money.
It is also well settled that anticipatory bail cannot be claimed as a matter of right but it is a concession and the same is to be granted by considering various factors.
For grant of anticipatory bail, the nature, gravity of offence as well as role of the accused is to be seen.

There are certain factors, which are to be considered while granting bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
9.

The offence like fraud or misappropriation or embezzlement etc, is committed with cool calculation and deliberate plan and in such types of offences, while granting bail, the nature and seriousness of an offence shall also be considered.

Applicant being Director of the firm, is alleged to have committed serious offence of forgery/misappropriation/embezzlement of the amount of the company and the investigation into the matter is still pending and, therefore, the applicant is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 10. At this stage, this Court cannot embark upon a detailed evaluation of the merits of the case.
In view of the allegations against the applicant, this Court is of the opinion that the present is not a case where the concession of anticipatory bail can be granted.
11. Accordingly, the application is rejected.
